evals.input: so the way the caching layer works is basically. you have your primary cache which is Redis and then behind that you have a secondary cache which is just in memory on each node. And when a request comes in it first checks the local cache and if it's not there it goes to Redis and if it's not in Redis either then it hits the database. The tricky part is invalidation because you have to invalidate both layers. and if you only invalidate Redis but not the local cache you get stale data for up to like 30 seconds which is the TTL on the local cache. We had a bug with this last month actually where. where prices were showing wrong for some users because of exactly this issue
evals.expected_output: The caching layer has two levels: Redis as the primary cache, and an in-memory cache on each node behind it. When a request comes in, it checks the local cache first, then Redis, then the database. The tricky part is invalidation — you have to invalidate both layers. If you only invalidate Redis but not the local cache, you get stale data for up to 30 seconds, which is the TTL on the local cache. We had a bug with this last month where prices were showing wrong for some users because of exactly this issue.

evals.input: So my grandmother used to make this amazing soup and I've been trying to recreate it for years. The base is pretty simple its just onions carrots celery the usual. But the secret was she would add a little bit of. I think it was miso paste which is weird because she was not into Asian cooking at all but someone must have told her about it at some point. And she would let it simmer for like hours. Not 30 minutes like the recipes online say but actually hours like three or four. And the texture would get so thick almost like a stew. I tried it last weekend and it was close but not quite right. I think maybe I need to use a different kind of potato because she used those waxy ones not the russet ones I had
evals.expected_output: My grandmother used to make this amazing soup, and I've been trying to recreate it for years. The base is simple — onions, carrots, celery. But the secret was miso paste, which is weird because she wasn't into Asian cooking at all, but someone must have told her about it. She would let it simmer for hours — not 30 minutes like the recipes online say, but three or four. The texture would get so thick, almost like a stew. I tried it last weekend and it was close but not quite right. I think I need to use a different kind of potato — she used those waxy ones, not the russets I had.

okay so the first capture is the current discount logic and then the second one is what Jake proposed as a replacement. I think Jake's version is better because it handles promo codes but I'd like to add validation for the discount not going below like 70 percent. also we should add tests for edge cases like negative prices

<capture id="1">def calculate_discount(price, tier):
    if tier == "gold":
        return price * 0.8
    return price * 0.95</capture>

<capture id="2">def calculate_discount(price, tier, promo_code=None):
